correctness.rationale: For Q=2^p-1, orbit points 2^k/Q (0<=k<p) are distinct. At x=1/Q only anchor 1 is trusted and maps to 2^(p-1)/Q; at all remaining orbit points anchor 0 is trusted and successive updates halve the numerator. The bounded open symmetric confidence set has one central and up to three mirrored positive bands (<=7 intervals). All included distances lie strictly in open bands; the forbidden odd integers lie outside by at least a positive gap, including p=2. Every local update has slope 1/2 and the p-return multiplier 2^-p. The strict gaps give an attracting neighborhood and robustness under small endpoint/anchor perturbations. A separate rational-integer checker verified selection and transitions for p=2..150 (11,324 orbit-state checks); no assertion of all-p truth rests on the finite checks. With fewer than three agents reciprocal two-agent averaging or single-anchor distance monotonicity forbids nonconstant cycles.
residual_risks: Robustness local only, not global; one distinct confidence set is chosen for each p.

originality.rationale: The November 1 full published theorem proves three agents with two stubborn anchors, an at-most-seven-component symmetric confidence set, an exponentially attracting least-p cycle for every p>=2, minimal three-agent threshold, and return multiplier 2^-p. Its confidence intervals are closed rather than open, but all periodic distances have strictly positive separation from endpoints; opening those intervals changes neither the itinerary nor local attraction, so the current open-set variation is a routine boundary modification. The October 18 earlier published result already proves arbitrary p, local attraction and three-agent minimality, though with a growing component count.
residual_risks: Earlier seven-interval proof has closed sets; equivalence relies on the explicit strict interior margins, not a literal identical set definition. No other surviving original mathematical claim found.
